analysis.title: Weekly Market Guide
key_insights: The week's headlines were a hot October CPI, Jensen Huang's resignation, global tech outages, an FAA nationwide ground stop and bank technical issues. The hot CPI led to talk of a 50bp Fed hike in December and a bounce in bond yields. The firm says headline volatility is adding to market volatility, with Technology hit hardest.

Technology is being sold on the post-election data center reaction, the Huang resignation and the technical outages. Investors are asking whether these events raise AI regulation and reduce AI momentum, risk-taking and spending. The firm says the direction may be right but the magnitude is easy to get wrong, because the AI ecosystem is more than one company and political hype can exceed legislative reality.

The firm argues Tech valuation has re-rated from 30x at the start of the year to 17x, with EPS growth of 42% in 2027 and 26% in 2028. It says the AI cycle may be elongated by a slower ramp-up. It still recommends balanced Tech allocations given concentration, leverage and vulnerabilities.

Short-term technicals are cautious. The Nasdaq and Technology failed to follow through on the bounce after the post-election pullback. Catalysts this week are major AI earnings, an IPO and the Trump/Xi (possibly Putin) meeting at the APEC Summit.

Investors are rotating exposures rather than selling outright, and diversified portfolios have held up well this year. Over 100 S&P 500 stocks have a negative 1-year beta. The firm expects more waves of rotation and favors Quality over High-Beta Momentum.

The firm sees a wave-midterm precedent. Both chambers flipped to the same party in 1946, 1954, 1994, 2006 and 2026. Those years averaged 3-, 6- and 12-month forward returns of +6.1%, +13.5% and +19.5%. The 2006 case returned +2.7%, +8.7% and +7.1%. Q4 in midterm years averages 6.2% against 4.1% in all years.

October retail sales control group rose 0.6% m/m against a 0.3% estimate, and September was revised up to 0.5% from 0.1%. The firm notes demand has held despite high interest rates and oil prices. It says falling oil over the past couple of weeks would support year-end spending and reduce inflation pressure and Fed hike odds.

The firm says the economic and earnings backdrop is healthy and the fundamental positives outweigh the headline-driven risks. Tech P/E is 16.5x, the lowest since pre-Covid. The equal-weighted S&P 500 P/E is in line with its long-term average.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term technicals are weak and headline risk is high, but valuation has compressed to 16.5x P/E and 2027/2028 EPS growth is 42%/26%. The firm recommends a balanced allocation.
The firm favors Quality factor exposure over High-Beta Momentum as rotation continues.

The firm says S&P 500 earnings estimates are seeing positive revisions on healthy growth. It does not state the revision magnitude in the text.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural AI forces are strong, valuation has re-rated from 30x to 17x, and EPS growth is 42%/26% in 2027/2028. The cycle may be elongated by a slower ramp-up.
tension_points.bear_case: The post-election data center reaction, the Huang resignation and tech outages may raise AI regulation and reduce AI momentum, risk-taking and spending. Technicals show weak follow-through.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The firm names no specific level. It says to watch for signs of potential reversal in Technology and for major AI earnings this week.
